technical_and_design_decisions: Use Maven as the standard build tool for all new and modified projects to align with existing Spring ecosystem conventions.

Implement uber-jar dependency override prevention using the Maven Shade Plugin with a custom dependency transformer that prioritizes core framework dependencies over external duplicates, and add a build-time validation step to fail the build if unresolved conflicts are detected.
Maintain backward compatibility with existing Spring XD SFTP module APIs during the port to the s-c-s repo to avoid breaking changes for existing users.
Design the RedisRule contract project as a fully standalone Maven module with zero dependencies on core s-c-d functionality to ensure complete isolation and reusability.
Align the processor OOTB module foundation with existing Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) module abstraction patterns to ensure consistency with the s-c-s-m repo's module loading mechanism.

Implement AetherModuleResolver offline mode using a configurable local file system cache directory that stores downloaded module artifacts, with fallback to remote Maven repositories only when the artifact is not present in the local cache.
Use an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap as the default storage mechanism for ModuleRegistry, with a defined extension point for future persistent storage implementations.
Implement ModuleRegistry CLI commands using Spring Shell to align with existing s-c-s command-line tooling conventions.
assumptions: All source code for existing components (s-c-d core, Spring XD SFTP module, existing RedisRule test coverage, s-c-s-m module loader) is fully accessible and has up-to-date documentation.
Existing CI/CD pipelines for the s-c-d, s-c-s, and s-c-s-m repos are already configured to build and test new Maven modules, so no new pipeline setup is required for this increment.
The local Maven repository path (~/.m2/repository) is used as the default cache location for AetherModuleResolver offline mode, and is configurable via environment variable or system property.
Existing test coverage for the RedisRule contract can be migrated to the new dedicated project without requiring significant rework of test logic.
The ModuleRegistry commands only need to support basic CRUD operations for module coordinates, with no advanced query, filtering, or batch operation requirements for this increment.
All development work will use Java 17 as required by Spring Framework 6.0, consistent with the existing version requirements of the target repos.
